Class ContainerRegion

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.menukit.api.panel.ContainerRegion
public final class ContainerRegion extends Object
The container region (7.4.0): on a container screen, the player's inventory never scrolls, and everything above it is one column that scrolls together. A chest, a shulker box opened below it and another one below that are one region, never a scroll area each. Mods put their containers' slot elements in it as sections, stacked top to bottom; there is one region per screen, however many mods add to it. It is never on the player's own inventory, survival's (InventoryScreen) or creative's (CreativeModeInventoryScreen), whatever a section's targeting says. 
ContainerRegion.section("mymod:opened-shulker", ModeScope.BOTH)
        .title(() -> Component.translatable("container.shulkerBox"))
        .source(() -> ContainerRegion.Source.of(session.box()))   // its texture and its name: "Lime Shulker Box"
        .content(shulkerGrid)            // SlotKit's slot elements, say
        .on(ContainerScreen.class)
        .order(10)                       // below the chest's own section (order 0)
        .visibleWhen(() -> session.isOpen())
        .declare();

Two panels

The containers and the inventory are two panels, each with its own frame: the container list on top, holding every section with its scrollbar inside its frame, and the inventory panel below it, MenuKit's gap between panels apart. The inventory panel is around the player's inventory, and moves only as the list grows. Scrolled content clips at the container list's own bottom edge.

Both are the screen's background (Panel.Builder.background()): drawn where the screen draws its own image, under everything else on the screen, vanilla's labels and slots and every other mod's widgets included, and claiming nothing, so another mod's button on either panel stays live and gets its clicks first. The region's own slots draw with the list, right after it, so another mod's button over one covers its item; they are cut at the list's edges.

The screen's bounds

The screen's leftPos, topPos, imageWidth and imageHeight are the rectangle around both panels, scrollbar lane included, set whenever the layout changes (the screen opening, a resize, a section opening or closing), never on a scroll. So a panel placed on the menu frame, another mod's buttons by the screen's edges and a recipe viewer keeping clear of the screen all see both panels, and a click in the gap between them with an item held is inside the screen, so it drops nothing. Vanilla's title is moved back by as much as the origin moved, so it stays put on screen, and the player's inventory slots and "Inventory" label go with the inventory panel. The slots are placed every frame from the slots the menu holds then, so one another mod puts in while the screen is open goes with the panel too, and putting the bounds back moves exactly the slots that were moved.

When the layout changes while the screen is open (a section opening or closing, the list starting to scroll), the screen is laid out again the way a window resize does (Screen.resize at its own size): every mod adds its widgets again from its own init hook, at the new bounds, so a button another mod placed by the screen's edges follows the panel it was by. Only then, never on a scroll, and once a frame however many sections changed. What a resize keeps is kept (the item on the cursor, the scroll, which sections are open, the anvil's name and the creative search); what it drops is dropped (which widget had focus). While the region is up, the screen's own background still runs, every mod's hook in it included, but vanilla's own container texture and the screen's title are left out: the two panels and the sections' titles are in their place.

Anchors

To put a button by one panel rather than by the whole screen, place it on CONTAINERS (the container list) or INVENTORY (the inventory panel) with an AnchorPanelAdapter. Either is absent on a screen the region is not on. 
Panel sort = Panel.builder("mymod:sort_chest").add(sortButton)
        .in(ModeScope.BOTH, Placement.around(ContainerRegion.CONTAINERS,
                PanelPosition.region(OutsideRegion.RIGHT_ALIGN_TOP))).build();
new AnchorPanelAdapter(sort);

To put a button by one section (a sort button for each box in the list), place it on anchor(sectionId): that section's rectangle, across the list, from the top of its title to the bottom of its content, moved by the scroll and cut at the list's viewport. It is absent while the section is hidden, scrolled wholly out of view or not on the screen, so the button hides with it, and comes back with it.

What the region does

  • Grows, centered, then scrolls. The container list starts at the screen's own container part, where vanilla's is, and grows with its sections. While the two panels fit, they stay centered on the screen as one block: the list's top moves up and the inventory panel down by half the growth each. Where one side has less room (a window too short for vanilla's own margins), that side holds and the other moves until the block is centered. Only once the block reaches the top and bottom margins does it scroll. Each panel moves at most a pixel per pixel of growth, so nothing jumps. It is never shorter than the screen's own container part (unless the screen is fitted(ModeScope, ScreenMatcher)), so a tiny window still shows vanilla's height, scrolling. A resize lays it out again.
  • The wheel, last, from anywhere on the screen. It scrolls the region only when vanilla and every other handler declined the turn: over a slot, a mod that moves items with the wheel (Mouse Tweaks, Inventory Profiles Next) keeps it, and a recipe viewer's list keeps its own; anywhere nothing wants it, the region scrolls. Nothing detects any mod.
  • A shift-click lands in view. A quick move into a slot of the region that is scrolled out of view scrolls it there. A quick move out of it (into the inventory) scrolls nothing.
  • Carrying an item to an edge scrolls it, faster nearer the edge.
  • Smooth. Pixels, never whole rows; a slot across the edge is drawn, hovered and clicked only where it shows (SlotClip).
  • MenuKit's scrollbar, in the screen's look, inside the container list's frame at its right while anything scrolls.

A section

Its ContainerRegion.Builder.title is drawn where vanilla draws a container's, and its ContainerRegion.Builder.content below it, at the region's content edge, where vanilla's grid frame is: a nine-wide grid at (0, 0) lines up with vanilla's own chest. Without a title the content starts at the top and draws whatever it likes there. A section draws its own slot frames. Hidden sections take no room. The screen's own container is a section too: whoever puts the region on a screen presents that screen's grid in it (SlotKit's SlotGroupElement.of(SlotGroupId) for a slot group, or SlotElement.builder().slot(address).build() for a single slot), since what is behind the container list is covered.

A section shows while its own ContainerRegion.Builder.visibleWhen holds and its content is visible: content that hides itself takes its section with it. A slot library's element for a slot group that is not on the open menu, or whose slots are all hidden, hides itself, so a section of such a group needs no condition of its own.

Resource packs

The two panels follow the resource pack's container art, as vanilla's own screen would under it: the container list takes each section's container texture, the inventory panel the inventory half of the screen's own. A section's container texture is its ContainerRegion.Builder.source's block's (a shulker box's for a shulker box, the chest's for a chest, ender chest or barrel), else its ContainerRegion.Builder.texture (vanilla's chest by default): its slot frames and its part of the list take that texture's look, down from a pixel above it to the next section's, the list's top and bottom with the first and last. It scrolls with the section. A section whose fill differs from the first one's, a block of its own, has its content moved down 2 px, so its title sits inside the block as vanilla's sits inside its art. MenuKit adds no color of its own: a section's color is the pack's. Text on the list keeps vanilla's colors wherever they read on the pack's fill, and takes one made from the fill where they would not.

Each section a slice of its own container's screen

Each section's part of the list, from its band's top to its bottom, is a slice of its own texture's panel: the list's left and right edges there are that texture's, and so is its fill; the list's top is the first section's, its bottom the last's. The outline runs on unbroken; where two sections meet, the colors change. With no pack every texture is vanilla's gray, and the list is MenuKit's panel as always.

Containers whose art a pack picks by block (OptiGUI)

With OptiGUI installed, a pack's rules can give a container art of its own by its block (a lime box), its name ("Ores"), its biome or its height. OptiGUI picks that for a whole screen, from the block that opened it; the region asks for each section's own. A section that knows its container says so with ContainerRegion.Builder.source, from the block entity it shows or the item it was opened from (ContainerRegion.Source.of(BlockEntity), ContainerRegion.Source.of(ItemStack)). One that doesn't is the screen's own container: it takes the block the screen was opened on (the one under the crosshair as it opened, when it holds a container the screen's size and the screen has its title), else what OptiGUI picked for the screen, as the inventory panel does. Without OptiGUI, no rules are read.

Titles and names

Title a section that is a vanilla container's with vanilla's translation key (Component.translatable("container.shulkerBox"), or the screen's own title, which is one) rather than a literal: packs whose art covers the title strip blank those keys, and with one container on the screen the section's title goes blank with vanilla's. With two or more sections shown, the player has to tell them apart, so a section whose title comes out blank shows a name instead, one packs don't blank: its ContainerRegion.Builder.name if it has one; else its container's, from its ContainerRegion.Builder.source (or, for the screen's own container, the block it was opened on): the name the player gave it, else its block's name in the player's language ("Lime Shulker Box"); else what vanilla's own English says for the title's key ("Shulker Box"). Sections that would show the same name are numbered ("Lime Shulker Box 1", "Lime Shulker Box 2"). The first section's title moves right, clear of the pack's top corner, where the pack decorates it.

Hidden sections

A section whose own condition doesn't hold this frame (ContainerRegion.Builder.visibleWhen, its mode scope, its screens) takes no room, and its slots are off on the client (Slot.isActive), so nothing draws, hovers or takes a click there, and a slot library's element leaves them out. A slot is a section's once the region has drawn it there; a container's own slot no section has drawn yet is the screen's own container's (its first section with no ContainerRegion.Builder.source). A shift-click that lands in a hidden section scrolls nothing: the section's ContainerRegion.Builder.onHiddenLanding runs instead, so its mod can show it.

The fitted frame

fitted(ModeScope, ScreenMatcher) declares screens whose list and inventory panel are one frame, as vanilla's image is, as tall as the shown sections need: shorter than the screen's own container part where they are smaller (a 3-row box shown on a double chest's screen), centered as the list is. Each shown section's slice of its own container art runs straight on into the inventory part, under a resource pack too. Sections as tall as a vanilla container's (a 3-row grid and its title) make that container's own frame, in the same place on screen, tab rows standing on it (ContainerTabs) and centered with it as they are on a vanilla screen's: switching between the two, with the same rows, moves nothing. To show one container at a time under tabs, as the creative inventory shows one page: 
ContainerRegion.fitted(ModeScope.BOTH, ScreenMatcher.only(ContainerScreen.class));
ContainerRegion.section("mymod:backpack", ModeScope.BOTH)
        .content(backpackGrid)
        .on(ContainerScreen.class)
        .visibleWhen(() -> shown == Shown.BACKPACK)
        .onHiddenLanding(() -> shown = Shown.BACKPACK)   // a shift-click into it shows it
        .declare();
ContainerTabs.tab("mymod:backpack", ModeScope.BOTH)
        .icon(() -> backpack.stack())
        .on(ContainerScreen.class)
        .selectedWhen(() -> shown == Shown.BACKPACK)
        .onClick(() -> shown = Shown.BACKPACK)
        .declare();

Sections for what opens at runtime

A section is declared ahead of time, so a mod that lets the player open as many boxes as they like would need one for each it might ever show. sections(String, ModeScope, Function) declares a kind of section instead: on a screen it is on, its keys are read every frame (any type with equals: a slot library's group instances, say), and each key has a section, built from the key the frame it first appears and kept for as long as it is there. A key that goes takes its section with it, and a new screen starts with none. They are sections like any other: titled, sourced, ordered and shown by what the builder sets, hidden ones' slots off, a shift-click into a hidden one running its onHiddenLanding. A kind's sections stack by their order, then by the kind's id, then in the order of the keys, so with the keys in the order they opened, the newest box is at the bottom. A tab per key is a keyed list of tabs over the same keys. 
ContainerRegion.sections("mymod:opened-box", ModeScope.BOTH, screen -> boxes.openOn(screen.getMenu()))
        .section((box, s) -> s
                .content(boxGrid(box))
                .title(() -> Component.translatable("container.shulkerBox"))
                .source(() -> ContainerRegion.Source.of(box.stack()))
                .order(10)
                .visibleWhen(() -> box.equals(shown))
                .onHiddenLanding(() -> shown = box))
        .on(ContainerScreen.class)
        .declare();

Declare from your client initializer: sections, and kinds of section, freeze with every other declaration.

    • anchor

      public static Anchor anchor(String sectionId)
      The anchor for one section, by its id ("mymod:opened-shulker"): its rectangle on screen, across the whole list (scrollbar lane included), from the top of its title to the bottom of its content, moved by the scroll and cut at the list's viewport. Absent while the section is hidden, scrolled wholly out of view, or not on the screen, so a panel placed on it with an AnchorPanelAdapter hides with the section. The section may be another mod's and need not be declared yet; asking twice for one id gives the same anchor. Ask from your client initializer, while declarations are open.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - when sectionId is not namespace:path
      IllegalStateException - the first time it is asked for after declarations froze

    • openedOn

      public static @Nullable ContainerRegion.Source openedOn()
      The container the open screen was opened on, the source its own sections (those with no source) take: the block under the crosshair as it opened, when it holds a container of the screen's size and title. null with no region screen open, for a screen opened from an item or by a key, on a double chest, and for a container the player named (the client never knows a placed container's custom name). Render thread.

    • scrolls

      public static boolean scrolls(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.Screen screen)
      Whether the container list on screen scrolls this frame, or a section's own grid in it does (a SlotScroll, or any scroll area that fits the room, giving rows back): true where the mouse wheel should go to the list rather than anything else a mod would otherwise do with it (switch tabs, say) while the cursor is over it. false while the region is not on screen, or no section shows. Render thread.

    • sections

      public static <K> ContainerRegion.Sections<K> sections(String kind, ModeScope scope, Function<? super net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?>, ? extends @Nullable List<? extends K>> keys)
      Starts a kind of section with one section per live key, for what opens at runtime: as many boxes as the player opens, each its own section, for as long as it is open. Its id is namespaced and unique ("mymod:opened-box"); scope is every one of its sections' mode scope. On a screen the kind is on, keys is read every frame with that screen; each key it gives has its section, built from the key, and the section goes when the key does. See "Sections for what opens at runtime".
      Parameters:
      keys - the keys open on a screen now, in the order their sections stack; any type with equals, a null or empty list for none
